mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a sustained RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following an INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY) coupled with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) signals accommodative monetary conditions, which boost equity valuations and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances under the specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a PAYEMS increase > 300,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a sustained GDPC1 decline.
